current.text: Charlotte got him from Minnesota in the LaMelo Ball trade.
He is projected to start at power forward in place of Miles Bridges. The projected Charlotte starters are White, Knueppel, Miller, Reid and Diabaté.
Charlotte's center plan is unclear. Diabaté, the rookie taken 14th, Kalkbrenner and Kai Jones are in the mix, which limits Reid's center minutes. He may play more power forward than center.
He is expected to play about 31 to 33 minutes, the most of his career. With Ball and Bridges gone, his usage should rise from about 22 to around 24.

Experts disagree on his upside. The newest call makes him a strong mid-round target in the 55 to 75 range, and earlier in category leagues. One expert gives him a better shot at the top 50 than at falling outside the top 100. Others rank him around 61 and see no upside beyond his tier.
He went for 14 USD in a recent mock auction.
Josh hoped to buy him for about 10 USD.
Charlotte plans to space the floor and take a lot of threes. That suits his floor spacing.
Charlotte plays 4, 3 and 4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. It has only 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum.

durable.text: He can play power forward or center and has F and C eligibility.
He is a very good floor spacer who brings physicality.
He makes clearly more threes than most forwards and centers.
His shooting is up and down, and he can be an inefficient scorer.
He is not a strong fantasy center. He does not boost FG% or give big rebounds.
He has not shown he can handle big usage.

note: Reid went for only 2 USD in our league last season as a bench player. Now he is a projected starter, Yahoo values him at 17 USD and ESPN at 20 USD, but average costs are only 4.2 and 7.7 USD and he went for 14 USD in a recent mock. A bid of 10 to 15 USD looks fair for a forward or center who adds threes, blocks and steals to any build, though his roughly 46% FG% on about 13 shots will not help FG%. Early in the season, check that he gets about 31 minutes, how many center minutes he takes from Diabaté and Kalkbrenner, and whether his shooting holds up with more usage.
